# Scale the Nerd Fonts glyphs by measurement instead of by eye

Every Nerd Fonts glyph used to be placed with four hand-tuned constants per source
(`x_ratio`, `y_ratio`, `x_diff`, `y_diff`). Sizes drifted by 34% between sources, vertical
centres by 23% of the em, and the pasted glyphs kept the advance width of the symbol font, so the
font carried 315 distinct advances while claiming to be fixed-pitch.

Nothing is tuned by eye any more. The scaling is derived from the fonts themselves.

* **Grid sources are mapped by their design grid.** Seti-UI, Devicons, Font Awesome Extension,
  Power Symbols, Material, Octicons and Codicons (about 8,700 glyphs) are drawn on a square grid
  that every glyph shares. That grid is now mapped onto the cell and the artwork is left alone, so
  the size the designer gave each icon relative to its neighbours survives. Correlation with the
  source sizes went from 0.42 to 1.00 for Material, from -0.04 to 0.97 for Devicons.
* **The remaining sources keep the upstream algorithm.** Font Awesome, Weather Icons, Font Logos,
  Pomicons and the Powerline sets are proportional, so their bounding boxes are measured and
  scaled, with the scale groups of the upstream `font-patcher` to hold related glyphs together.
  The hand-maintained scale groups for Material, Octicons and Codicons are no longer needed and
  have been dropped.
* **Advance widths are normalised.** 315 distinct advances become 2: one cell for hankaku, two for
  zenkaku. `post.isFixedPitch` is now true in fact and not only in the table.
* **Glyphs that overflowed the cell**: 1,824 of them did, now 17, all of which are Powerline
  separators that overlap their neighbours on purpose.
* Material draws its letters, digits and f-keys at text size because it also ships boxed variants.
  Standing alone they were unreadable, so each of those families is measured against itself, and
  the alphabet is levelled to one width: `alpha-m` and `alpha-w` no longer tower over the rest.
* **Codepoints that Unicode calls one cell wide are now one cell wide.** `23FB`-`23FE`, `2B58` and
  `2665` used to ask for two. `2630` asked for one where Unicode says two, which let the next
  character be painted over.

The generated files are 30% smaller as a side effect of rounding coordinates.

No codepoint is added, moved or dropped, and no glyph outside the Nerd Fonts sets is touched.
